problem: "Use whichever condition is easier to observe" is too compressed. A student may not see that it means choosing between multiplying by P(B) with P(A|B) and multiplying by P(A) with P(B|A).
fix: Say it plainly: the rule can be written as P(A∩B)=P(A|B)P(B) or as P(A∩B)=P(B|A)P(A). Pick the version whose conditional probability you can estimate or observe more easily.

problem: "This chapter builds the formula, tree diagrams ..." is a roadmap sentence of the kind the series style avoids; it tells the reader about the chapter instead of teaching the idea.
fix: Replace with a statement of content, for example: 'The formula below, the tree diagram for two-stage draws, and the difference between independent and mutually exclusive events all follow from this one definition.'
